title: Correctness of AND-normal conversion
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables, and let $x : \\mathrm{Fin}\,n \\to \\bbf_2$ be an assignment. The AND-normal circuit obtained from $c$ evaluates at $x$ to the same Boolean value as $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables
$x$ is an assignment of Boolean values to the $n$ variables
replaced:
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables — a tree of literals combined by AND and
OR gates — and let $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$ be an assignment to those variables.
Converting $c$ into strictly alternating AND-normal form and evaluating the resulting
normal-form AND circuit at $x$ yields the same Boolean value as evaluating $c$ directly
at $x$.
